text:
maria_pr: Hey team — quick alert. FT picked up our benchmark blog and published a piece citing a 2.5x throughput improvement vs baseline. Our canonical number is 2.1x (see blog link). Need PR + eng to align and decide whether to ask for a correction or push an update. :eyes:

sam_engineering: Thanks for flagging. That 2.1x is the verified median across our tests; 2.5x came from a misread of the 95th percentile. We should correct the quote.

annie_marketing: Agree we should ask for a correction. What's the fast path? Do we do an email to the reporter or a public note?

maria_pr: Reporter contact is in the byline (emma.roberts@ft). I can send a correction note now — want the exact line to propose.

sam_engineering: Suggested wording: "Correction: Our published benchmark median throughput improvement is 2.1x versus baseline; the 2.5x figure referenced the 95th percentile and was misstated." Short and factual.

kevin_ceo: +1. Keep it factual, no defensive language. If they push back, we can offer the raw methodology table and test artifacts.

annie_marketing: Also: if they update the article, we should push a small social correction thread linking to our blog + a short note to partners who syndicated the piece. I'll draft the tweet thread after PR confirms the correction. :loudspeaker:

olivia_ops: Quick ops note — if we send the methodology package we should redact internal hostnames and account IDs. I'll scrub anything sensitive before sharing.

maria_pr: Good catch. I'll send the correction email now and attach a redacted results table. Draft below — please quick-review.

maria_pr: "Hi Emma — thanks for covering our benchmark. Quick correction: the blog's headline-metric should read 2.1x median throughput improvement vs baseline; 2.5x referenced the 95th percentile and was inadvertently cited as the median. We're happy to provide the redacted methodology table for verification. Best, Maria (PR, Redwood Inference)"

sam_engineering: LGTM. Add a one-line link to the methodology section in the blog for transparency.

annie_marketing: Drafting the short social copy. Proposed: "Correction: FT updated an article referencing our benchmark — the median throughput improvement is 2.1x (read our methodology + full results) [link]." Will queue after confirmation.

maria_pr: Sent to Emma. Subject: "Correction request: benchmark median throughput" — email sent  — pinging here for a timeline.

press_bot: reporter_email_delivered: true

maria_pr: Emma replied: "Thanks — we'll update the article and note the correction later today." She asked for the redacted table attachment (sent) and a one-line correction we can paste.

kevin_ceo: Great. Once FT updates, marketing can amplify. Also prep an internal note for Sales so they have the corrected stat for customer calls.

annie_marketing: Will prepare a 2-sentence internal comms and an updated slide for the sales deck. ETA 45m.

olivia_ops: I've scrubbed the table and dropped it into a secure share link (internal only). maria_pr, can you confirm you used that version?

maria_pr: Confirmed — used the scrubbed table. Emma confirmed receipt.

sam_engineering: Logged the small methodology clarification in the repo so future PRs reference the percentile language explicitly.

annie_marketing: All right — once FT posts the correction, I'll post the social note, update the tweet copy in Buffer, and ping partners. Will post here when live.

maria_pr: Update: FT published the correction and appended a notice to the article. Link: https://www.ft.com/example-corrected (shared for records).

press_bot: article_update_detected: https://www.ft.com/example-corrected

annie_marketing: Live social copy posted and scheduled for partner syndication. Shared the internal comms doc in #marketing-assets.

kevin_ceo: Thanks everyone. Nice fast coordination.

maria_pr: Closing loop — saved thread and added to comms postmortem notes. If anyone sees further pickup with the old number, tag me and we'll follow up. :white_check_mark:
